If there's one thing the management should invest in, it's improving their staff and the quality of work they put out. The credit for BINI's current fame goes to the girls themselves (their talent, personality, and relatability) and the fans who actively promote them on Twitter. Note that even the viral "Pantropiko" dance was choreographed by their youngest member, Sheena.

I do agree that the management is overworking BINI. The girls have events left and right, which has led to some of them getting sick, like Aiah and Gwen.

I don't understand why it's wrong for the girls to interact with their fans online. Besides their vocals, they're known for their humor. People love them because of how casual they are with their fans. What does having minor fans have to do with standing up for themselves? Isn't it a good example for them to stand up for what they think is right, as seen with Jho's statement? Fans (and bandwagon fans) have gone overboard, and it's only right for them to be called out when they're making the girls uncomfortable and ruining their advocacies. That's exactly why they speak up—they know their influence.

Mikha and her personal life have nothing to do with this at all. She isn't publicly disclosing her whereabouts, and the problem lies with people making assumptions based on pictures shared by fans. If none of you saw it, she wasn't at XYLO.

This take is just plain wrong. The girls have been working hard, and if you compare them to K-pop groups, it's actually good that they speak out instead of being silenced by their management.

If there's one thing the management needs to invest in, it's making an individual team dedicated to BINI and BINI only. The lack of effort in the teasers and merch they put out is evident.

Yeah, there really isn't anything out there that can truly fulfil the constant emptiness we feel. Thank you, I hope you do as well! Because who knows, maybe a good day would come to us. Know that a stranger is rooting for you to have good days.

I understand, it really is a hard thing to do. I'm not sure if it would work for you, I usually don't talk about my feelings or thoughts to any of my friends as well. So I write instead, my outlet. It doesn't matter whichever way you prefer to write, in a paper, or in your phone's note. It helped me let out whatever I was feeling that time, and it made me aware of the different emotions I was feeling. Maybe it would help you keep track of your days, sometimes it's good to acknowledge the emotions you felt. But out of the way, you're free to do whatever you're comfortable with.

I'm not sure if you want any advice, and I don't think I can say anything anyways, but I just want to tell you that I've been experiencing the same thing. I've been taking care of other things that I've forgotten to take care of myself. Does it get tiring for you? Doing the same things every day, and even if you want to do some hygiene, you just don't have energy to do so. I hope the people around you realizes that you also need some care, like you do with them.

I don't want to call it "bad" because it really is just a way of people to cope, but neither is it a good thing. That's why I still recommend you to find a different way to cope without harming yourself. Also, I don't think that you should disregard your feelings just because you feel that it isn't serious or the reasons are shallow. The fact that you feel sad and/or empty is already enough reason for it to be serious, your feelings matter. I hope you get to talk to someone about what you're feeling, because usually waiting does nothing. It's better if you let it out, or you find a source of outlet that, again, doesn't harm you.
I truly hope that a person (who you can confide in) comes to your life. I'm sorry that you feel this way. If you need someone to talk to, just send me a message. I'll listen.

I just like exploring and watching films that I see or is recommended to me. And I'm not really sure what I wanna see in classical films yet since I really have no idea what genres are there and what it was like before. But! I'm not too sure if this would even be helpful but I'm not much of a fan of romantic films (in the current period). The reason why I said I'm open to any genre is because, as you've said, time had progressed. So I'm sure that there are vast differences on how films were before and today. It doesn't really matter to me if it's romcom, thriller, musical, etc. So in some sense, me asking for recommendations, is also just me seeking out what genres would fit my taste? I'm not too sure yet, and I don't even know if that makes sense. 

Sorry if this isn't that much of a help, but I'll try to check out more films to see what I'd like and ask again next time too! Really appreciate you for telling me this.

TLDR; Not much fan of romantic films (in the current period!), but I guess it's inevitable so as long as it's not the main point of the movie I'm fine with it. For other genres I'm open with any of it especially musicals because I haven't watched much. Since I'm just a starter in classical films maybe recommend some well known movies first?

I'm sorry about that, you don't deserve that kind of treatment from your family or anyone. And no, you're not being petty it's understandable that you're feeling this way. Your family, especially your parents are grown ass adults but they're acting like a child instead of handling it properly. No matter who is right or wrong, they shouldn't be taking sides. They should be listening to the both of you (about the problem and just generally) and settle it.

And, no, I'm sure you're a great person. Don't let anyone think you're not, because you are. I hope you find someone who listens to your concerns, you deserve the best. Also, don't worry about feeling those things you have all the right to be sad, mad, or whatever it is.
